content:
Apple TV's current lineup is quite strong, with flagship titles including "Slow Horses," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and the new comedy "Brothers" starring Matthew McConaughey. But there's more good stuff coming — here's a complete guide to all Apple TV October premieres.

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

"The Last First: Winter K2," directed by Amir Bar-Lev, tells an intricate, thrilling, and moving story that delves deep into the extreme mountaineering industry and its evolving culture. The story focuses on a 2021 expedition during which mountaineer John Snorri Sigurjónsson (from Iceland) and the Pakistani father-and-son team Ali and Sajid Sadpara set out to become among the first to summit K2 in winter, when conditions are at their harshest. Along their perilous climb, they encounter all manner of people — influencer climbers with their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and celebrated Nepali mountaineer Nims with a team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers to K2's frozen peaks and unpredictable weather, revealing an unexpected and layered story of strategy and determination, class and barriers, money and power — all unfolding between life and death.

The Sisters Grimm (Season 2)

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphan sisters navigate a town filled with fairy tale characters — heroes and villains alike — while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure, delivering important lessons for viewers of all ages.

Small Prophets

  • Date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy that tells the story of eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley) — who has been living an extraordinarily mundane life since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago. He works at a hardware store, visits his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and waits for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe calling for rainwater, horse dung, and a touch of alchemy. Michael takes the recipe and, with a healthy dose of skepticism, begins crafting homunculi — magical sprites that can predict the future — hoping they can answer his biggest question: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie

  • Date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

Based on the classic Mattel toy, "Matchbox The Movie" is a fast-paced, globe-trotting action adventure about a group of childhood friends who have settled into stable lives — until CIA undercover agent Sean (John Cena), their long-missing former leader, suddenly returns to their small town and inadvertently drags them into a wild, world-saving international chase.

Tenzing

  • Date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

"Tenzing" is based on the true story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a tale that has been little told. A gifted Himalayan mountaineer, he partnered with New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) to become among the first to summit Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing gains expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe) as an ally. Together, they convince Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing deserves to be a full member of the British expedition, not just someone servicing their logistics. Where Western climbers see "Everest" as a peak to conquer, Tenzing reveres "Chomolungma" as a sacred snow goddess. The ensuing climb unfolds amid tensions of background, class, and ambition, while battling the mountain's deadly hazards. But at the top of the world, empires, status, and desires fall away, leaving two men from the margins bound by mutual respect and trust — for Tenzing, the journey is also the fulfillment of a lifelong dream and spiritual calling.

Where's Wanda? (Season 2)

  • Date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about Dedo and Carlotta Klatt — whose 17-year-old daughter Wanda vanished without explanation months ago. Desperate, the police have made no progress, so the family takes matters into their own hands, using surveillance equipment acquired with help from their tech-savvy son Ole. Posing as utility company workers, they install bugs around the neighborhood, then expand to half the community — and discover that behind closed doors, nobody is who they appear to be.

Nocturne

  • Date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series follows Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber) — a veteran homicide detective burnt out on Philadelphia's mean streets, who moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania seeking a quiet life. But when the town and his family are threatened by a cunning, twisted serial killer, Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. When the hunt for Jurek's last missing victim forces Jonah to send his goddaughter, FBA agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), to confront Jurek personally — how far is Jonah willing to go?

New Episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers," and More

Apple TV also has new episodes dropping throughout October across several currently airing series, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": Jason Sudeikis-starring comedy, with new episodes through October 7
  • "Last Seen": Crime thriller, with new episodes through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": Acclaimed British spy series, with new episodes through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": Sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton, with new episodes through October 30
  • "Brothers": Comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, with new episodes through November 4

Which Apple TV October release are you planning to watch? Share your picks in the comments.

Apple TV costs USD 14.99 per month (approximately HKD equivalent), or you can subscribe via the Apple One bundle.
